result.title: Learning from Self-Generated Responses: Reliability--Uncertainty Self-Distillation for Reasoning
result.summary: Reference solutions and question-specific rubrics are not always available to guide the teacher in self-distillation. A large language model's own solution attempts offer an alternative, but their quality is difficult to assess in open-ended tasks without automatic correctness checks, and even correct attempts can involve uncertain token predictions. We propose Reliability--Uncertainty Self-Distillation (\method{}) to learn from these attempts. The same model serves as teacher and student: the teacher receives the question and completed attempt, and the student matches the teacher's token-level predictions using a question-only prompt. \method{} weights each attempt's distillation loss by additively combining judged reliability, estimated from a self-judge's score and confidence, with student predictive uncertainty. Across eleven reasoning benchmarks, \method{} outperforms all five baselines in average accuracy, reaching 70.47\% on Qwen3-4B and 76.69\% on Qwen3-8B (8.90 and 2.10 percentage points above the base models). Data and code are available at https://github.com/JP-25/RUSD.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出可靠性—不确定性自蒸馏 RUSD：同一模型兼任教师与学生，教师输入问题与已完成的解答尝试、学生仅凭问题匹配其 token 级预测，并按自评得分与置信度得到的可靠性及学生预测不确定性加权蒸馏损失，在 11 个推理基准上评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 属纯文本自蒸馏，不直接研究 LVR；其按可靠性、不确定性为监督信号加权的做法，可能为 latent 轨迹训练与贡献分配提供可核查线索，但能否迁移到视觉证据筛选尚不明确。
